# 英文原文

作者：Nicholas Dulait  
来源：https://x.com/nicholasdulait/status/2102312923943063837?s=46

the only guide you need to print cash with GEO
The complete 80/20 of GEO fits in two steps:
Identify the queries that trigger an AI answer (AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity).
Do traditional SEO on those queries.
There is no secret step 3.
That's the point Paul, my co-founder at ChatSEO, made this week on a podcast with Delgado.
Branding, E-E-A-T, citations: all of it ranked sites in Google ten years ago, and it's exactly what gets a brand surfaced in ChatGPT today. The name changed, the job didn't.
Struggling to grow your website's traffic?
Try the first agent built by a real SEO/GEO expert (7 days for free) ✅
So instead of debating the term, here are the concrete tactics that came out of that conversation. Everything is applicable this week.
1. Aim for the citation, not just the backlink
This is the most important mindset shift. For two years now, every time we place a link, the question is no longer "which backlink" but "which citation". Sometimes you put more value into the brand mention than into the link itself.
The logic: if you were Google, what would you look at to separate a real brand from a site gaming the algorithm? Citations. Including brand mentions inside YouTube videos, a signal far harder to fake than a purchased link.
Bold prediction from the podcast: link building agencies will become PR agencies.
2. If you buy links, filter like a consultant
Two concrete criteria so you don't buy junk:
The site ranks and gets traffic. If Google already gives it credit, the odds that your $60 link actually passes authority go up.
Verified Google Search Console traffic, not the Semrush estimate. Third-party estimates can be gamed. GSC can't. Some platforms now display it. That's your filter.
3. The video + short combo: four placements from one piece of content
The most actionable tactic of the podcast. Paul ran it on the name of a big US competitor:
One YouTube video targeting "[brand] review". Title = the exact keyword. The title on YouTube works like the title tag in SEO: keyword in, you rank. Keyword out, you don't.
One short with the same title.
Result: #1 on YouTube for the query (near-zero competition), ranking in Google, and the two videos become a double source shaping the AI Overview answer. Four placements, one piece of content to produce.
Is that "GEO"? No. It's YouTube SEO with a good title. But that's what influences AI answers, not a $200/month GEO module.
4. One perfect page, then replicate
If your strategy runs on a keyword pattern (SEO consultant + city, agency + CMS, software + industry), the hard work is the first page. Build it properly: SERP analysis, expected page type, structure.
Then replicate. SEO consultant Paris becomes Lille, Marseille, Lyon. Same structure, local data. AI makes replication nearly free, but only if the initial template is good.
This is literally the feature we spent the most time on in ChatSEO: it checks the SERP, identifies the expected page type, and builds that first perfect page with you. And here's the honest part: for the replication step, you don't even need it. Once the template is right, any AI can decline it. Pay for the hard page, not the copies.
5. Be skeptical of GEO tracking tools
Not because they're scams. Because the data doesn't exist. There is no reliable search volume database for AI queries, nothing like Google Ads data to pull from. So these tools blast prompts into the AIs to see if you show up, without knowing whether anyone actually types those prompts.
They're doing the best they can with what the market gives them. But know what you're measuring: an estimate built on hypothetical queries. Don't build your strategy on it.
It's also why ChatSEO runs on your real Google Search Console data instead of synthetic prompts. Real queries, real impressions, real clicks. Boring data beats hypothetical data.
The common thread
Reread the five points. Citations, link selection, titles, page templates, skepticism about data. Not a single tactic here existed after ChatGPT that didn't exist before it. That's why GEO is a bullshit term: it sells you the idea that you need to start from scratch, with new experts and new tools, when the SEO skills you already have apply directly.
To everyone who thinks SEO is dead: someone is currently selling them GEO. And in the end, SEO is what they'll get.
That's how we built ChatSEO. No separate GEO module. The agent identifies your queries, checks the SERP and applies these methods, in Google and in AI answers alike. Because it's the same job.
